section: Reservation - constitutional basis, Indra Sawhney, creamy layer, EWS reservation, promotion in reservation

accepted.s: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Articles 15(6) and 16(6) to provide reservation for Economically Weaker Sections?
accepted.x: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment, enacted in January 2019, inserted Articles 15(6) and 16(6) for EWS reservation.
accepted.tq: Use the amendment-number and provision pairing to distinguish closely related constitutional amendments.

accepted.s:
With reference to reservation for Economically Weaker Sections, consider the following statements:
1. It may extend up to 10 per cent.
2. It is available only to persons covered by SC, ST or OBC quotas.
3. It is in addition to the existing reservation quotas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: EWS reservation may extend up to 10 per cent and is additional to existing quotas. It is meant for persons not covered by SC, ST or OBC reservation.
accepted.tq: Split the options by checking the exclusion condition in statement 2.

accepted.s:
The constitutional provisions relating to EWS reservation are applicable to which of the following institutions or sectors?
1. Central educational institutions
2. Private educational institutions
3. Posts under the Central Government
4. State Governments on a compulsory basis
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The 103rd Amendment provides EWS reservation in central educational institutions, including private institutions, and in posts. Its implementation is not mandatory for State Governments.
accepted.tq: Identify the statement that overstates the constitutional obligation by using a compulsory application to States.

accepted.s: For determining EWS eligibility, which one of the following combinations correctly represents the income and asset criteria stated for the purpose?
o: Annual family income below ₹5 lakh, land below 2 acres and flat below 800 sq ft
Annual family income below ₹8 lakh, agricultural land below 10 acres and flat below 1,000 sq ft
Annual family income below ₹8 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and flat below 1,000 sq ft
Annual family income below ₹10 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and flat below 1,500 sq ft
accepted.x: The stated EWS criteria include annual family income below ₹8 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and a flat below 1,000 square feet.
accepted.tq: Match the numerical threshold with the associated land and dwelling limits.

accepted.s: The Supreme Court judgment in Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India was delivered on which date?
accepted.x: The Supreme Court upheld the 103rd Amendment in Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India on 7 November 2022.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the amendment year and the date of the later judicial decision.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the decision in Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India:
1. The 103rd Constitutional Amendment was upheld by a 3:2 majority.
2. Chief Justice U.U. Lalit dissented.
3. Justice S. Ravindra Bhat dissented.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The EWS amendment was upheld by a 3:2 majority, while Chief Justice U.U. Lalit and Justice S. Ravindra Bhat were among the dissenting judges.
accepted.tq: Check the judicial split first, then verify both named dissenting judges.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the 50 per cent ceiling referred to in the context of reservation from EWS reservation?
o: The ceiling applies to backward-class reservations, whereas EWS reservation was provided additionally under Articles 15(6) and 16(6).
The ceiling applies only to reservations in promotions.
The ceiling applies exclusively to EWS reservation.
The ceiling was abolished by the 103rd Amendment.
accepted.x: The 50 per cent ceiling discussed in this context relates to backward-class reservations. EWS reservation was introduced additionally through Articles 15(6) and 16(6).
accepted.tq: Separate the general reservation ceiling from the constitutional source of EWS reservation.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the expression “Backward Classes” in the Constitution is correct?
o: It is exhaustively defined in Article 15.
It is defined in Article 340 itself.
It is defined only in the Fifth Schedule.
It is not defined in the Constitution.
accepted.x: The Constitution does not define the expression “Backward Classes”; constitutional provisions instead provide mechanisms concerning their identification and welfare.
accepted.tq: Test the exact constitutional status of a frequently misattributed definition.

accepted.s: The 27 per cent reservation for OBCs in Central Government jobs came into effect from which year?
accepted.x: The 27 per cent OBC quota in Central Government jobs came into effect from 1993.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of implementation in jobs from the later year of implementation in central educational institutions.

accepted.s: The Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006, providing 27 per cent OBC reservation, came into force in:
accepted.x: Although enacted in 2006, the Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act came into force in 2007.
accepted.tq: Separate the enactment year from the commencement year.

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the principal objective of the Oversight Committee headed by M. Veerappa Moily in 2006?
o: To prepare the Central List of Scheduled Tribes
To implement OBC reservation by expanding seats so that general-category seats did not shrink
To identify the creamy layer among SCs and STs
To abolish reservation in Central educational institutions
accepted.x: The Oversight Committee headed by M. Veerappa Moily planned implementation through expansion of seats, thereby protecting the existing number of general-category seats.
accepted.tq: Use the committee’s stated implementation purpose rather than its year alone.

accepted.s: The expansion of seats contemplated by the Oversight Committee for implementing OBC reservation was approximately:
accepted.x: The committee contemplated raising the total number of seats by about 54 per cent, in a phased manner, so that general-category seats would not be reduced.
accepted.tq: Match the committee’s implementation plan with its approximate quantitative figure.

accepted.s: The National Commission for Backward Classes examines requests relating principally to:
o: Appointment of judges to the Supreme Court
Inclusion in or exclusion from backward-class lists
accepted.x: The NCBC examines requests for inclusion in or exclusion from the lists of backward classes and advises on such matters.
accepted.tq: Ask which constitutional body would handle the specific administrative request.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes Article 15(5)?
o: It provides for appointment of a commission on SEBC conditions.
It provides reservation in promotions for SCs and STs.
It provides for special provisions for SEBCs, SCs and STs in admissions, including private institutions, except minority institutions.
It provides for carry-forward of backlog vacancies.
accepted.x: Article 15(5), inserted by the 93rd Amendment, permits special provisions for SEBCs, SCs and STs in admission to educational institutions, including private aided and unaided institutions, while excluding minority institutions.
accepted.tq: Distinguish admission provisions from promotion, carry-forward and commission-related provisions.

accepted.s: The 93rd Constitutional Amendment is associated with which one of the following provisions?
o: Constitutional status for the NCBC under Article 338B
Reservation for EWS under Articles 15(6) and 16(6)
Identification of the Central List under Article 342A
Special provisions for admission under Article 15(5)
accepted.x: The 93rd Amendment inserted Article 15(5), enabling special provisions for admission of SEBCs, SCs and STs, including in private educational institutions other than minority institutions.
accepted.tq: Use the amendment–Article pairing to avoid confusing the 93rd, 102nd and 103rd Amendments.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Article)
A. Article 15(4)
B. Article 16(4A)
C. Article 16(4B)
D. Article 340

List-II (Subject)
1. Carry-forward of backlog vacancies
2. Commission on conditions of SEBCs
3. Special provisions for SEBCs, SCs and STs
4. Reservation in promotion for SCs and STs with consequential seniority

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Article 15(4) concerns special provisions for SEBCs, SCs and STs; Article 16(4A) concerns promotion for SCs and STs; Article 16(4B) concerns backlog vacancies; and Article 340 concerns a commission on SEBC conditions.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure Article 340–commission pair and then complete the reservation pairings.

accepted.s: Under Article 342A, which one of the following is correct?
o: The President specifies the Central List of SEBCs, while States retain their own lists.
The Governor specifies the Central List of SEBCs, while States have no separate lists.
The NCBC alone specifies both Central and State lists.
The Supreme Court specifies the Central List of SEBCs.
accepted.x: Article 342A provides for specification of SEBCs for the Central List by the President, while States retain their own lists.
accepted.tq: Use the authority–list distinction to separate Central List and State List powers.

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Article 15(6) — EWS reservation in education
2. Article 16(6) — EWS reservation in public employment
3. Article 338B — National Commission for Backward Classes
4. Article 342A — Central List of SEBCs
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Articles 15(6) and 16(6) concern EWS reservation in education and public employment respectively; Article 338B concerns the NCBC; and Article 342A concerns the Central List of SEBCs.
accepted.tq: Verify each Article–subject pair independently before selecting the coded combination.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indra Sawhney judgment:
1. Caste may be the main criterion for determining backwardness.
2. Total reservation should ordinarily not exceed 50 per cent.
3. The creamy layer among OBCs should be excluded.
4. Reservation for OBCs was extended to promotions as a general rule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Indra Sawhney accepted caste as a possible main criterion, prescribed the general 50 per cent ceiling and excluded the creamy layer. It confined reservation to initial appointments and did not extend it to promotions as a general rule.
accepted.tq: Locate the single reversal in the statement dealing with promotion.

accepted.s: According to the ruling in Indra Sawhney, the 50 per cent ceiling on reservation may be exceeded:
o: Whenever a State Government considers it desirable
accepted.x: The judgment laid down that total reservation should ordinarily not exceed 50 per cent, though extraordinary circumstances may justify an exception.
accepted.tq: Watch for the distinction between an ordinary rule and an absolute prohibition.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the ruling in Indra Sawhney regarding carry-forward vacancies?
o: Carry-forward is allowed, but it must operate within the 50 per cent ceiling on a year-by-year basis.
Carry-forward is prohibited in every situation.
Carry-forward applies only to EWS vacancies.
Carry-forward is unlimited and is calculated only once in a decade.
accepted.x: Indra Sawhney permitted carry-forward of vacancies, subject to the 50 per cent ceiling being applied year by year.
accepted.tq: Combine the carry-forward rule with the year-by-year ceiling rather than treating either as absolute.

accepted.s: The reservation contemplated in Indra Sawhney was confined primarily to:
o: Private employment, and not public employment
Political representation, and not public employment
accepted.x: The judgment confined the reservation policy under consideration to initial appointments and held that it did not apply to promotions.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the two stages of public service—appointment and promotion.

accepted.s: The permanent statutory body for backward-class lists directed by the Supreme Court in Indra Sawhney subsequently became the:
accepted.x: The permanent statutory body directed for backward-class lists subsequently became the National Commission for Backward Classes.
accepted.tq: Match the judicially directed institutional role with the body that performs it.
